head: L7 H6
definition: All local maxima, no height/rank selection: p[d]>p[d-1] and p[d]>=p[d+1]. Peak density is peak count/(queries*bin width). Mean height is sum of weights at peak apex tokens/peak count. Their product is the mean contribution at peak tokens. Alltoken mean includes peak flanks and troughs too. Native full-softmax probabilities; same20heldoutdocs,128latequeries/doc. Bins16..1022; age1023 used as neighbour. Each plotted series divided by its own value in the16..31reference bin only, to compare proportional changes. Original attention is never locally renormalized.
interpretation: For all local maxima, peak density is nearly constant across near/far bins; mean peak height drops similarly to total mean attention. Peak apex mass share near55.3%,far56.1%, so this is a substantial, not exhaustive, mass accounting. This does not contradict rarity of top8 or >=1% peaks, which is a different selection; no causalRoPEmechanism proven.
